narrative.overview: Twenty tactile, brightly coloured toys sitting on one warm shelf. The shelf is the shared neutral: a soft stone page, one rounded typeface, generous corners. Each toy (game) carries exactly one saturated brand colour and its own voice.
keyCharacteristics: One warm-neutral page, one accent per game

rules.name: The One Brand Rule
rules.body: A screen shows one game's brand colour, never a neighbour's.

rules.name: The White Ink Rule
rules.body: Brand fill takes white ink for every game, including the light fills; the contrast cost is a knowing owner decision.

rules.name: The Neutral Chrome Rule
rules.body: Exit, back and How to Play never take a brand colour.

rules.name: The Split Title Rule
rules.body: A menu title is never one flat colour: neutral half plus brand half.

rules.name: The Gel Stays On The Shelf Rule
rules.body: gel-btn belongs to the menu and lobby buttons only.

dos: Do use the game's single brand colour for Play, active pills, ON toggles and focus.
Do keep Header, Stage and Controls in one max-w-sm column.
Do use .gel-btn on menu buttons only, with .gel-btn-light on pale fills.
Do animate transform and opacity only, and honour reduced motion in JS loops.
Do write UK/Australian spelling and let personality live in the words.
donts: Don't make it corporate or SaaS-clean.
Don't put emoji on action button labels or in setting-card titles.
Don't put a brand colour on exit, back or How to Play.
Don't add transition-all, ease-in, or a third overlay pattern.
